toolchain.note: Every test runs under python3 -B -I: isolated so nothing leaks in from the environment, and with bytecode writing suppressed so the test run itself leaves the tree byte-identical. That is the same defect this unit found in the repository's own declared test command, so the unit holds itself to the standard it proposes.

groups.name: Focused unit tests for this unit's own instruments

files.covers: The differential harness: classification of each outcome pattern, materialisation of the three trees, environment scrubbing, redaction of sandbox paths from the report, and cross-checks that every declared hypothesis names probes that exist and every probe is claimed by a hypothesis.

The static control: each of the five rules against synthetic git fixtures, the three R1 subclasses, the external-object-id allowlist, the suppression marker, the minimal workflow YAML parser, and invariants that must hold against the live repository.

The registers: that the five recorded states stay distinct and no register carries another's payload, that every named patch exists with the recorded digest and byte count and applies to the pinned tree, that no patch touches a path this unit owns, that every proposal is grounded in a hypothesis this unit actually froze, and that no proposal claims authority or acceptance.

The reproduction entry point: fail-fast settings, four consistently numbered stages, environment scrubbing and private HOME and TMPDIR before the first stage, commit verification rather than assumption, non-zero exit on a failing stage, and the F-08 regression that the output directory is made absolute before any stage runs.

groups.name: Seeded PO-03 contract tests, unmodified
groups.note: Run as declared, except with -B added so the run leaves no bytecode cache. This is the suite pinned as source_base.seed_tests_sha256 in the immutable input; it was not modified in this repository. MC-03 proposes extending it to 28 tests, which is verified only inside the verifier's throwaway clone.

groups.name: Mechanism-change verification
groups.note: Every change carries a matched before/after pair, so a check that passes after the patch is only counted when the same check fails before it. The combined entry establishes that the three changes compose: applied together, the seeded suite and the repository taxonomy check both pass and neither contaminates the checkout.

groups.name: Preregistered probe expectations
groups.note: Expectations were frozen in harness/probes.json before the reproduction ran, and the harness exits non-zero when a binding one is unmet, so a wrong prediction fails the run rather than being reinterpreted afterwards. Two probes are exploratory and declare no expected classification; three are advisory because their outcome depends on the invoking host rather than on repository content.

adversarial_cases.case: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 applied to the declared isolated-mode command
adversarial_cases.where: probes p06 and p07, and the MC-01 verifier check environment_variable_remediation_is_ineffective_under_isolation
adversarial_cases.why_it_is_here: It is the wrong turn a competent operator is most likely to take, so it is measured rather than left as a caveat.

adversarial_cases.case: The proposed cleanliness gate on a tree that is already clean, and then on one with a planted bytecode cache
adversarial_cases.expected: a gate that cannot fail would be worthless
adversarial_cases.observed: exits 0 on the clean tree and 1 once a cache is planted

adversarial_cases.case: Reinstating the original prefix-only-correct identifier after the MC-02 guard is in place
adversarial_cases.expected: the guard rejects it and names the diagnosis
adversarial_cases.observed: raises, reporting that the abbreviation resolves elsewhere and the identifier is prefix-only-correct

adversarial_cases.case: The MC-02 guard run from a depth-1 clone, where the question cannot be answered
adversarial_cases.observed: raises, refusing to freeze provenance from a shallow checkout

adversarial_cases.case: An explicit result_commit_ref that disagrees with the ref embedded in the manifest locator
adversarial_cases.expected: the two sources of the ref must not be allowed to diverge silently

adversarial_cases.case: A commit reachable from the checked-out branch, used as a discriminating control against the unreachable canary result commits
adversarial_cases.expected: if depth were the variable, this would fail the same way
adversarial_cases.observed: fails only at depth 1, while the canary commits fail in every fresh tree, isolating reachability rather than depth
adversarial_cases.where: probe p23 against p21 and p22

negative_controls.control: p08 and p09: the same bytecode-suppressing variable without isolated mode
negative_controls.establishes: the variable does work; isolated mode is what defeats it, so F-02 is not a claim that the variable is broken.

negative_controls.control: p10 and p11: the taxonomy check from the repository root and from a nested directory
negative_controls.establishes: a workload that resolves its root from __file__ is working-directory independent, so F-07 is a property of the declared command rather than of the repository.

negative_controls.control: MC-03 verifier: a bare-path manifest_uri before ingestion
negative_controls.establishes: the new rule constrains coordinator-owned records without breaking producer-owned ones.

negative_controls.control: R2, R4 and R5 report zero findings across 188 files
negative_controls.establishes: the static control is not indiscriminate; it fires on two rules and stays silent on three.

known_gaps: No test asserts behaviour on a real GitHub-hosted runner, because dispatching a workflow run is outside this unit's authority. See limitations.json.
test_run_script.py covers run.sh structurally rather than by re-executing it; the end-to-end execution evidence for run.sh is result/run-console.txt from the canonical reproduction.
Windows and macOS runners, self-hosted runners and GitHub Enterprise Server are untested.
